method: Every finding below was demonstrated with a command run in the worktree at branch openspec/trace-requirements-to-contracts. reviews/consensus-plan.json was ignored as instructed. Round 5's findings were preserved to reviews/review-findings-plan-r5.json before this file was overwritten.

findings.title: The merge_group union-and-block rule rests on a premise the spec itself refutes two lines later, and makes the exclusions file unsatisfiable: no single traceability-exclusions.yaml can make both blocking runs green
findings.description:
THE FALSE PREMISE. spec.md:567-569 justifies blocking on union mode with: 'Inside a merge group the same directory holds precisely the changes that are landing, because the evaluated branch *is* the integration branch plus the batched pull requests.' The subordinate clause states the correct fact and the main clause draws the opposite conclusion from it. A merge-queue branch is main PLUS the batched PRs, so openspec/changes/ there contains everything main carries. Measured: `git ls-tree --name-only origin/main openspec/changes/ | wc -l` returns 34 -- 33 in-flight change directories plus archive/. Four lines earlier the same paragraph states the correct rule for push-to-main ('holds every in-flight change whose plan has merged and whose implementation has not'), which is exactly the set a merge-group branch inherits. The same false claim is in design.md:438 and 462 and tasks.md:614.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT COSMETIC. Task 4.2b opts gen-eval-framework into reverse enforcement in this very change. Three in-flight, plan-merged, unimplemented changes on main carry gen-eval-framework spec deltas -- extract-gen-eval-package (5 ADDED + 1 MODIFIED), factory-missions-architecture-alignment (3 ADDED), rename-descriptor-model-levels (2 ADDED), verified with git show. Under union mode those ~10 requirements enter gen-eval-framework's effective requirement set, no operation cites them (their implementations have not landed), reverse enforcement is on, so the sweep exits non-zero. Under the operator's decision that run BLOCKS. This change therefore cannot pass its own merge_group check, and neither can any unrelated PR queued afterwards, until all three of those changes land. That is the exact failure the deleted rationale ('the union admits requirements nothing has built yet ... which is why that run reports and never blocks') existed to prevent; the fix commit did not refute that reasoning, it asserted it does not apply on a branch where it demonstrably does.

THE CONTRADICTION IS UNSATISFIABLE, NOT MERELY COSTLY. There is no exclusions file that makes both blocking runs green, because the two blocking runs impose opposite requirements on the same artifact:
  - merge_group (union) requires openspec/contracts/gen-eval-framework/traceability-exclusions.yaml to exclude extract-gen-eval-package's requirements, or it fails reverse completeness (spec.md:224-228).
  - pull_request (--change trace-requirements-to-contracts) requires it NOT to, because those identifiers are not in that mode's effective set. Scenario gen-eval-framework.other-changes-are-invisible (spec.md:404-411) is explicit: 'WHEN a citation or exclusion names a requirement that exists only in a different in-flight change's spec delta THEN the gate SHALL fail AND the failure SHALL state that the requirement is not in the effective requirement set.' The stale-exclusion rule (spec.md:124, scenario 152-157) says the same thing again.
So the file must both contain and not contain those entries. Whichever way it is authored, one of the two BLOCKING runs is red, permanently, with no remedy available to any author.

FIX REQUIRES AN OPERATOR DECISION -- do not let an implementer pick. The options are visible from here: (a) merge_group unions only the change directories the merge-group diff touches against event.merge_group.base_sha, rather than every directory on the branch -- this restores the 'precisely the changes that are landing' premise as an actual rule instead of an assertion; (b) merge_group blocks but reverse enforcement is evaluated only over requirements from deltas the merge group introduces; (c) merge_group is non-blocking and the pull_request run remains the only blocking one, reverting half the decision. Whichever is chosen, the premise sentence must be replaced in all three artifacts (spec.md:563-571, design.md:436-439 and 458-464, tasks.md:611-616), not just the rule.

findings.title: 5.7c is the change's only acceptance criterion and it exercises only the --change invocation, so nothing in the plan can detect R6-F1 before it reds the merge queue
findings.description:
Task 5.7c is labelled 'the acceptance criterion the change otherwise lacks' and asserts 'a non-zero result here means merging reds main immediately.' Its command is `check_traceability.py --scope capability --change trace-requirements-to-contracts`, and a note insists 'pass --change explicitly.' That is the pull_request invocation. It never runs the merge_group invocation (capability scope, --change omitted, union), which under the operator's decision is the run that actually gates the merge.

The consequence is that the plan's single green-light check is blind to the one configuration that will fail. The claim 'a non-zero result here means merging reds main' has an unstated and now false converse: a ZERO result here does not mean merging is safe, because the union-mode blocking run is a different effective requirement set and, per R6-F1, will exit non-zero on the same tree. proposal.md:232-233 has the same gap -- 'The full sweep on the merge candidate fails on violations in opted-in surfaces and reports the rest' is stated as an acceptance criterion for failure behaviour, with no criterion that the merge candidate PASSES under the invocation that gates it.

FIX: 5.7c must record the exit code of BOTH merge-candidate invocations on the merge commit -- `--scope capability --change trace-requirements-to-contracts` and `--scope capability` bare -- and both MUST be zero, with the note stating why the bare run is the one the merge queue executes. This is worth fixing independently of how R6-F1 is resolved: whatever rule merge_group ends up with, the acceptance criterion must exercise it, or the plan ships a gate whose blocking path was never once run against real artifacts. Note also the ordering trap in the existing note -- 5.7c depends on 4.2b, so the human authoring the exclusions file needs both exit codes in front of them, not one.

findings.title: design.md's 'The blocking job derives its change id from the diff' paragraph is unqualified and contradicts the merge_group rule stated 30 lines above it in the same decision
findings.description:
The paragraph at design.md:470 is written as the universal behaviour of 'the blocking job': it says the change id is derived from the diff, that its absence is a SKIP, and that 'Two touched directories is a genuine ambiguity and fails rather than guessing' -- none of it qualified by event. Under the operator's decision all three statements are pull_request-only; on merge_group there is no derivation, no SKIP path, and the ambiguity rule explicitly does not apply (design.md:436-441 says so). This is the same defect shape the author corrected three instances of in 5979e25f (the rule updated, the prose explaining it left stale), in the artifact the author edited.

Not blocking on its own: spec.md:527-543 and tasks.md:657-670 both state the per-event split unambiguously, and an implementer following either gets it right. But this paragraph is the most operational-sounding prose in D12, and wp-wiring's dispatch text points implementers at D12. Add the pull_request qualifier to the heading and to the ambiguity sentence.

(Verified: `grep -n 'The blocking job derives its change id' design.md` -> 470; `grep -n 'if:' .github/workflows/ci.yml` -> only 451: `if: failure()`, so the surrounding factual claims about ci.yml still hold.)

findings.title: job-runs-on-every-declared-event can be satisfied by a test that never resolves the sweep job, and its second clause bans the wrong guard
findings.description:
B2 verdict for the other four new scenarios: all distinguishable. merge-group-unions-and-blocks, push-to-integration-branch-reports, the narrowed ambiguous-change-fails and the generalised unresolvable-base-fails-not-skips can each be driven through the ci.yml bash fragment with a synthetic GITHUB_EVENT_NAME and event payload (the harness tasks.md:645-650 names, modelled on test_gen_eval_mode_selection.py), and each fails before the job exists.

job-runs-on-every-declared-event is weaker in two specific ways. First, it is an absence assertion, and `grep -n 'if:' .github/workflows/ci.yml` on the unmodified tree already returns exactly one hit (`if: failure()`), so a test phrased as 'no job carries an event-excluding if:' passes today, before any work. It only becomes falsifiable if it first resolves the sweep job by its id and asserts it exists. Neither the scenario nor task 5.7 names the job id, so the implementer is free to write the vacuous form -- the same shape as round 5's `test -f` step that `touch` satisfied. Second, the AND clause bans only 'a condition that excludes it from merge_group'; a guard of `if: github.event_name != 'push'` satisfies the scenario literally while violating the THEN clause above it.

FIX: name the job id in task 5.7 (e.g. `traceability-sweep`) and require the test to (a) locate that job in ci.yml and fail if absent, (b) assert the job has no `if:` key at all rather than enumerating forbidden conditions.

findings.title: Union mode's 'every spec delta present under openspec/changes/' does not exclude openspec/changes/archive/, leaving the implementer a coin-flip over 128 archived deltas
findings.description:
`git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main openspec/changes/archive/ | grep -c 'specs/.*/spec.md'` returns 128. openspec/changes/archive/ is literally 'under openspec/changes/', so the rule as written admits every archived delta into the shadow set. Nothing in spec.md, design.md, tasks.md or work-packages.yaml says otherwise: `grep -n 'changes/archive' design.md tasks.md work-packages.yaml` returns nothing. Whether the implementer globs openspec/changes/*/specs/*/spec.md or openspec/changes/**/specs/*/spec.md is currently undetermined by the plan and unobservable in review.

Consequence today is small -- archived ADDED requirements are already in the archived spec, so re-shadowing is idempotent, and only one archived delta carries a REMOVED/RENAMED section (`git grep -l '## REMOVED Requirements' origin/main -- 'openspec/changes/archive/*/specs/*/spec.md'` -> 1, 2026-03-21-improve-worktree-management), whose removals are already reflected in the archive. So this is a nit, not a critical. But it is a free fix: state the glob as the immediate children of openspec/changes/ excluding archive/, in spec.md:511-513 and in task 3.16.

findings.title: B3 checked and clear: push:[main] is the integration-branch trigger the spec assumes, and per-event non-blocking is expressible in Actions
findings.description: ci.yml declares exactly `push: branches: [main]`, `pull_request:` (unfiltered), `merge_group:` (unfiltered), matching the spec's three-event set with main as the integration branch. No expressibility problem exists: 'non-blocking on push' does not require job-level continue-on-error and its required-check interactions -- the run step can exit zero on the push path (event-conditioned `|| true`, or a report-only flag on the gate), which satisfies the scenario's 'SHALL exit zero' literally. `grep -rn continue-on-error` over the change artifacts returns nothing, so the plan does not mandate the problematic mechanism. fetch-depth: 0 is already required by tasks.md and wp-wiring's description, which covers the pull_request base.sha fetch. Nothing here is blocking.

findings.title: B5 verified clean: wp-matrix's two template paths exist, the verification step fails on the unmodified tree, and generated copies are correctly excluded
findings.description: Both write_allow additions resolve to real files (openspec/schemas/feature-workflow/templates/change-context.md and skills/plan-feature/install_assets/openspec/schemas/feature-workflow/templates/change-context.md, both 2210 bytes). Running the verification command verbatim on the current tree exits 1 and prints both filenames -- it fails before the work, as required. `find . -name change-context.md` confirms the only other template copies are under .agents/ and .claude/, and both are absent from write_allow and from the grep argument list, so they are excluded rather than accidentally required -- correct, since install.sh regenerates them. Minor note only: the assertion is residue-based (grep for 'Fill .*Contract Ref'), so a reword that keeps Contract Ref in the fill list would still trip it while a reword that drops the word 'Fill' would pass; that is acceptable given it demonstrably fails now.

findings.title: B4 verified clean: wp-wiring's pointer to task 5.7 is specific and the retained summary is accurate
findings.line_range: wp-wiring description (3684 chars, under the 4000 limit)
findings.description: The description says 'Task 5.7 carries the full per-event table -- follow it exactly' and then restates all three event behaviours correctly in one sentence each (pull_request derives --change from the diff and blocks; merge_group omits --change, applies no ambiguity rule, and blocks; push on main omits --change and is non-blocking), plus the two rules most easily lost in a trim: do not add an `if:` excluding a declared trigger, and an unresolvable base where one is required is an ERROR never the SKIP. What did NOT survive the move is the literal base expressions (github.event.pull_request.base.sha / github.event.merge_group.base_sha); those are in task 5.7 and the pointer to it is explicit and by task number, so an agent that follows the first sentence has them. Nothing load-bearing was lost. Note that R6-F1, if resolved by changing the merge_group rule, invalidates this summary -- the description is one of the artifacts that must be re-edited.
